category_title: Elementary student with ASD engaging in head-banging and arm-biting during transitions
minimal_context: Jake is finishing an independent puzzle activity and transitioning to a waiting period at his desk in the classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Jake, independent work time is over. Please put your puzzle away and wait at your desk until we transition to the next activity.

STUDENT: (Puts the puzzle away and sits at his desk, left alone and unoccupied.)

TUTOR: I need to help the other students right now. Just sit there by yourself for a few minutes.

STUDENT: (Sitting alone without any activities during the transition period, Jake begins to bite his arms.)

TUTOR: Jake, remember we are just waiting quietly right now.

STUDENT: (Continues to bite his arms and begins head-banging, engaging in self-injurious behavior that causes physical injury.)

options.A: Provide extra time for Jake to complete independent puzzle activities and offer flexibility with timelines during transition periods in the classroom.
options.B: Develop critical consciousness through multicultural curricula addressing authentic issues of race, ethnicity, social class, and disability during independent work and transition periods.
options.C: Put effort into improving Jake's study techniques and increasing his ability to take initiative during independent work and transition periods in the classroom.
options.D: Develop a behavior intervention plan based on reinforcement strategies like NCR and DRO, and include progress monitoring to track Jake's self-injurious behavior over time.
